paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can fall, and the fall is not the end of you. The speaker says, "Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light." (Micah 7:8) And notice the speaker doesn't dodge the blame, either: "Because I have sinned against Him…" (Micah 7:9). Honest about the mess AND sure of the light. Both at once. That's the move.

Why can the speaker be so sure? Because of who God is. The message asks, "Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity…" (Micah 7:18), and then says He "does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion." (Micah 7:18) Delights! He's not doing forgiveness with a sigh and a clipboard, friend. And the picture gets even better: "You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea." (Micah 7:19) I've been stuck in the back of a drawer, so believe me, I know how good it is to be found.

So what do you do with that today, baker? Quit hiding your worst moments, and bring them to the God who delights in loving devotion. His promises aren't brand new either. The message ends with Him showing "faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old." (Micah 7:20) Same God, same promise, and that's why the ovens stay warm.
